transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Occupational health sent me. They’re worried my weight is too low for the kind of work I do—running presses, fabrication, that sort of thing. I guess they think it’s dangerous. I didn’t really see it that way… I just thought I was getting leaner, more disciplined.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or experienced any significant weight loss recently?

I mean… I guess I don’t get that hungry. Most days it’s just coffee before the early shift, maybe half a protein bar at lunch. Then after yoga I’ll have a small bowl of vegetables. Eating more than that just… makes the day feel like it’s getting out of control.
Have you noticed that you don’t take as much pleasure in things as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once enjoyed?
I’m not sure. I don’t really think about it that way. I still do what I need to do… work, yoga, chores. I guess I don’t have much time for “enjoying” things.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless lately?
I don’t know… not really sad, exactly. I’m just tired a lot, and I try not to dwell on things. Hopeless sounds… stronger than what I’d say.
Have you noticed that you’re not getting pleasure out of things that used to make you happy, even a little bit?
I don’t know… maybe a little, but I haven’t really been paying attention to that. Things just feel like things I have to get through.
Can you think of something you used to enjoy doing, and do you still get any pleasure out of it?
I don’t know… I used to maybe like going out with people, or working on little projects. I still do some things, but I can’t really say if I enjoy them. I just… do them.
Would you say that you’ve been feeling down or low most days, even if it’s not exactly sadness?
Maybe… some days, yeah. I don’t really think of it as “low,” though. More like I’m just getting through the day.
Can you think of a specific activity or moment where you used to feel a sense of enjoyment or satisfaction, and do you still feel that way about it?
I’m not sure. I guess maybe finishing something at work used to feel good, like I’d done it right. Now it’s more just… done. I don’t really think about whether I feel satisfied.
Can you think of any activity that you used to look forward to, even in the past, and do you still feel any sense of anticipation or pleasure when you do it now?
I don’t really know. I can’t think of anything I look forward to like that… not clearly. I still do things, but it’s more out of habit, I guess.
Would you say that you no longer feel any pleasure or satisfaction in activities you used to enjoy, even a little bit?
I don’t know if I’d say no pleasure at all. It’s just… muted, maybe. I don’t really notice it much.
How long have you felt this way about not really getting pleasure or satisfaction from things you used to care about?
I’m not really sure. It’s hard to put a time on it… I guess it’s been a while, but I haven’t really been keeping track.
Would you say that these feelings of things feeling 'muted' and going through the day without much pleasure have been present most days for at least two weeks at a time?
I don’t really know. Maybe… I mean, it probably happens a lot, but I haven’t been marking it off by weeks or anything. It’s hard for me to say for sure.
Would you say that you’ve completely stopped getting any enjoyment out of things you used to like, even things that used to make you feel a little good?
I don’t think completely, no. I mean… sometimes there’s a little something, maybe. It’s just not much, and I don’t really pay attention to it.
Would you say that you’ve experienced a loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, even things that were once meaningful or important to you?
I don’t know if I’d put it that strongly. Some things just don’t feel like they used to, I guess… but I haven’t really thought about whether it’s “loss of interest” or anything.
Would you say that your mood has been low or flat most of the time for at least the past two weeks, even if it’s not intense sadness?
I’m not really sure. I guess I can feel kind of flat sometimes, but I haven’t been keeping track like that… two weeks, most of the time—I don’t know.
Would you say that most days, for at least the past two weeks, you've felt a low or flat mood that doesn't seem to go away, even if it's not intense sadness?
I don’t know. I guess I do feel kind of flat some days, but I’m not sure I’d say it’s most days or that it doesn’t go away. I haven’t really been tracking it.
Would you say that on most days, for at least two weeks in a row, you’ve felt a low or flat mood that doesn’t seem to go away, even if it’s not intense sadness?
I mean… I still don’t really know. I have days where I feel kind of muted, I guess, but saying it’s most days for two weeks straight feels… I’m not sure. I haven’t paid that close attention.
Would you say that you’ve had a low or flat mood nearly every day for at least two weeks in a row?
I really can’t say for sure. I know I feel kind of flat sometimes, but nearly every day for two weeks… I don’t know.
Would you say that you’ve completely stopped getting any enjoyment out of things you used to like, even things that used to make you feel a little good?
I don’t think… completely stopped, no. I mean, I don’t really pay attention to that kind of thing much, but I wouldn’t say nothing ever feels okay.
Would you say that you’ve noticed a clear change in your interest or pleasure in doing things, even things that used to give you a little enjoyment?
I’m not sure. I guess I haven’t really noticed a clear change like that… things just feel kind of the same, or I don’t think about it much.
